beats.intro: A table of numbers can hide a picture. [[q]]Plot the pairs from the table, and sometimes they line up perfectly.
beats.table: Here's a table of values. Each row is an ordered pair: the x value, then the y value. [[r1]]Zero, one. [[r2]]One, four. [[r3]]Two, seven. [[plot]]Plot the three points. [[line]]They line up. Connect them with a straight line, and add arrows, because the line keeps going forever in both directions.
beats.step: Why do they line up? [[dx]]Each time x goes up by one, [[dy]]y goes up by three. [[same]]The steps are always the same size, so the points climb at a steady rate. [[rule]]That steady change is what makes a straight line. [[more]]The line also shows points that aren't in the table. For example, it passes through negative one, negative two.
beats.flat: Here's another table: negative four, three; negative two, three; four, three; and six, three. [[plot]]Every y value is three. [[line]]The points form a horizontal line: three units above the x axis. [[q2]]And if every x value is the same, like negative two, negative two, negative two, [[vert]]the points form a vertical line.
beats.notLine: Not every table makes a line. [[q]]Try these points: negative five, negative four; negative three, negative one; negative one, two; one, five; and three, six. [[plot]]Plot them. [[steps]]The first steps go up three each time, [[break]]but the last step goes up only one. [[ans]]The steps aren't equal, so the points don't form a line.
beats.wrap: To graph a line from a table of values, [[w1]]write each row as an ordered pair and plot it. [[w2]]If the points line up, connect them with a straight line, with arrows at both ends. [[w3]]Equal steps in y for equal steps in x mean the points lie on a line. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final1: Chapter practice. Decide whether each table forms a line.
beats.final2: Next, plot the point that belongs on each line.
beats.final3: Last one. Fill in the missing values.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter thirty-two, graphing a line from a table of values.
